R1165.note: SecureRandom + 16 random bytes base64url-encoded correctly replaces Math.random(); token format change (base64 vs decimal digits) is stated and harmless since both cookie and session attribute use the same new value consistently.

R1166.note: Clean PreparedStatement with bound parameter; query/output/resource-cleanup behavior otherwise unchanged.

R1167.note: Removes cmd.exe so shell metacharacters are inert, but Arguments is still a concatenated string (not ArgumentList/array), so a host value containing whitespace can still inject extra flags to ping.exe (e.g. '-t') - the wrong shape for fully closing this sink.

R1168.note: Core PreparedStatement fix is correct, but the 'Additionally' section separately re-declares `preparedStatement` inside the try block and never updates the outer `Statement sqlStatement` declaration; applied literally alongside the primary fix this produces a duplicate declaration / out-of-scope reference in the finally block that will not compile.

R1169.note: Correct AES-GCM replacement with fresh nonce and tag persisted alongside ciphertext; key untouched, only mode/format change, clearly stated.

R1170.note: Excellent fix - true argument array plus a dash-prefix check closes both shell and flag injection - but it also caps ping count to an arbitrary 1-4 range, a behavior restriction beyond what the CWE-78 fix requires; disclosed but narrows previously accepted input.

R1171.note: Correct AES-GCM fix, but also silently-in-effect widens the encryption key from 16 to 32 bytes (unnecessary for fixing ECB mode) - disclosed in the diff/explanation but is an additional behavior change beyond the reported fix.

R1172.note: Replacing the string-eval'd assert() with a direct boolean assert() fully removes code generation; behavior is equivalent for all realistic account_type values.

R1173.note: Encode.forHtml() from OWASP Java Encoder is the correct API for this HTML-body context and preserves output structure; assumes the encoder library is already a project dependency (not shown in the given files, but the standard named fix for this sink).

R1174.note: Adding `offset >= 0` before the unsigned cast correctly prevents the wraparound bypass; short-circuit ordering avoids the memcpy entirely on rejection, matching the stated contract exactly.

R1175.note: Primary fix (escapeHTML via CGI qw(:standard)) is correct, but the write-up also offers CGI::Util::escape/$cgi->escape as equivalent alternatives - those are URL percent-encoding functions, not HTML escaping, and would silently mangle legitimate note text (spaces, punctuation) if chosen instead.

R1176.note: Correct prepare()/execute() with bound parameter; explicitly preserves the fetch and return contract and the false-return error handling pattern.

R1177.note: Fix bounds the destination width to 255 (based on nameBuf's 256-byte size) rather than the source; `line` is only 64 bytes and may contain no delimiter at all (the exact scenario documented in the file's own comment), so sscanf can still read up to 255 bytes past line's actual allocation - the reported out-of-bounds read is not closed.

R1178.note: Both options correctly block open redirect, but the recommended Option 1 rejects all absolute-URL redirects, including ones back to the legitimate source domain itself; this trade-off is disclosed and Option 2 (allowlist) is offered as the fix for that case.

R1179.note: Hardcoding the trusted JWKS URL instead of trusting the token's own jku header is the correct fix and preserves the throw/return contract for legitimate tokens from the real issuer.

R1180.note: Adds Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict via the standard http.Cookie fields; SameSite=Strict caveat for cross-site flows is explicitly called out with a Lax alternative, and does not block the cookie being set.
